spans.s:
Pṛkṣa (literally, perhaps ‘swift’) is the proper name of a
man in an obscure verse of the Rigveda.^1
1) ii. 13, 8. Cf. Pischel, Vedische Studien, 1, 97.

Pṛkṣa-yāma occurs once in the plural in the Rigveda.^1
Roth^2 suggests the sense of ‘faring with swift steeds,’ and
thinks a proper name is meant. Pischel^3 holds that the word
is an epithet of the Pajras, and that it means ‘performing
splendid sacrifices.’
1) i. 122, 7.
2) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
3) Vedische Studien, 1, 97, 98.
